minutes.headline: APDC will pursue an RFP, grants, and National Register listing for the old primary school; no vote on its fate.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met remotely, approved the December 16 minutes and the amended January 12 workshop minutes, and discussed the old primary school after the Select Board workshop. Members agreed to pursue a new request for proposals, grant money and National Register listing, and a town campus or green-space use. They also covered the district inventory map, missing district signs, and the Brooks House.

votes.motion: Accept the December 16, 2020 minutes as presented
Accept the January 12, 2021 workshop minutes as amended

votes.outcome: passed, all four members said aye on roll call

budget_items.topic: Demolition of the old primary school
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled that a report from a couple of years ago put the demolition cost at a figure, and said it has likely risen with inflation.

budget_items.topic: Possible grants for the old primary school
budget_items.what_was_said: A member offered to research grants and contact the Massachusetts Historical Commission, citing a small grant as an example.

budget_items.topic: Past sale price of the Jones house
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled the asking price for the Jones house and the lower price it eventually sold for, saying an RFP asking too much needs to be lowered.

decisions.decision: The chair asked Colin Dwyer to look into the previous RFP and draft a new one for the old primary school.
Members agreed to pursue three options: town campus, green space, and redevelopment, with National Register listing and grant research alongside.
Tony Nicastro agreed to research grants, including contacting the Massachusetts Historical Commission.
The chair will follow up with the planning board on the Brooks House and will draft a letter or attend a meeting.
The next meeting was set for Wednesday February 24th at 7 o'clock.

what_happened.line: Members agreed to pursue a new request for proposals, grant research and National Register listing for the old primary school, with no vote on its fate.
The chair asked Colin Dwyer to look into the previous RFP and draft a new one for the old primary school.
Tony Nicastro agreed to research grants, including contacting the Massachusetts Historical Commission.
The chair will follow up with the planning board on the Brooks House and may draft a letter or attend a meeting.
Members approved the December 16 minutes and the amended January 12 workshop minutes.

why_it_matters: The old primary school is a town-owned building, so whether it is reused, sold or demolished can affect town costs and how the site is used; a new RFP and grant money are the routes the commission is choosing for now.
Any later sale, demolition or redevelopment would need decisions by other town bodies, and residents may be asked to weigh in at a Select Board meeting or Town Meeting.
